predecessors.name: Ebla
predecessors.text: the infobox's 'Preceded by: Ebla'; Ebla itself became a vassal of Yamhad under Yarim-Lim I

ledger.x: c. 1810 BC: Sumu-Epuh founds Yamhad at Aleppo. Infobox 'Established: c. 1810 BC (Sumu-Epuh)'; 'The kingdom emerged at the end of the 19th century BC'; capital Halab (Aleppo).

ledger.cp: Shamshi-Adad I's kingdom (the page does not name Tuttul's previous holder)

ledger.x: c. 1752 BC: Yamhad at its peak. ledger.x: c. 1650 BC (bridged): Yamhad's vassal kingdoms fall away. 'By the time of Yarim-Lim III in the mid-17th century BC, the power of Yamhad declined due to internal dissent'; Hattusili I's Syrian campaigns begin 'with Alalakh in the second year of his Syrian campaigns c. 1650 BC'. The page gives no year for the loss of…
ledger.cp: Syrian vassal kingdoms (Ebla, Mamma, Ugarit, Alalakh, Carchemish)

ledger.x: c. 1650 BC: Hattusili I destroys Alalakh. 'Alalakh fell starting with Alalakh in the second year of his Syrian campaigns c. 1650 BC' (Alalakh page: 'Fire and Conflagration' around 1650 BC; one reading 1628 BC). The Hittites did not keep it (the hittites dossier has no Hatay cell before 1345).

c. 1524 BC: Parshatatar of Mitanni annexes Halab. The last king, Ilim-Ilimma I, 'whose reign ended c. 1524' when Parshatatar of Mitanni, 'who annexed Halab', orchestrated a rebellion. Idrimi 'conquered Alalakh c. 1517 BC, and the name Yamhad then ceased to be used'.
c. 1524 BC: the kingdom of Yamhad ends. The infobox gives 'Disestablished: c. 1517 BC', the date the name ceased with Idrimi's conquest of Alalakh.

wars.name: Yarim-Lim I's conquest of Tuttul
wars.outcome: Tuttul conquered in 1777 BC and Zimri-Lim installed as governor; he regains Mari's throne after Shamshi-Adad I's death around 1776 BC and marries Yarim-Lim's daughter Shibtu.
